text.p: The Turkish lira closed weaker at 90,420 to the dollar on Friday after Thursday's 90,170 on dollar/mark gains and a higher central bank dollar rate for banks' currency transfers despite a cash shortage.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory monthly foreign currency transfers at 90,150 lira at the opening, up from 89,900 at Thursday's close. But the central bank raised the rate further to 90,350 lira in line with the dollar's gains.
The central bank injected a total 34.86 trillion lira into the market to relieve the liquidity shortage.
It funded 10.86 trillion lira by buying seven-day repos from banks at an average annual rate of 73.66 percent on the open market.
The bank also funded 24 trillion lira in overnight cash at 75 percent on the interbank. Overnight rates also traded at 74.75 percent. Central bank's overnight lending was 30 trillion on Thursday.
In the t-bill market, t-bill yields dropped by one-to-two points across the board on buying in outstanding papers because they will be exempt from the new tax.
The new resources package presented on Thursday by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan included the withholding tax on interest income from Treasury bills and bonds to be issued with a 1997 maturity.
The tax will go into effect after a related government decree is published in the Official Gazette and will not be retroactive.
"Yields continued to ease today amid activity in existing papers," said one banker.
The yield on the most actively traded March 26, 1997 paper, fell to 125.64 percent from Thursday's 126.87 percent average.
The second most heavily traded March 12 paper yielded 124.82 percent after 126.11 on Thursday.
